label: Drew on Ibn Arabi’s polysemic Sufi hermeneutics to defend open interpretive pluralism
description: Writing early monographs on Ibn Arabi, Abu Zayd recovered classical Sufi openness to infinite textual meanings against literalist closure.
dialecticalTension: Links medieval mystical polysemy to modern linguistic hermeneutics.

label: Applied structural semiotics and communication theory to Qur’anic discourse analysis
description: Using Saussurean linguistics and Russian/Czech semiotics, Abu Zayd analyzed revelation as a communicative code grounded in 7th-century Arabic culture.
dialecticalTension: Synthesizes modern semiotics with Mu’tazilite linguistics of the created word.

label: Pioneered Humanistic Qur’anic Hermeneutics grounded in historical linguistics and ethics
description: Abu Zayd argued that reading scripture as humanly intelligible discourse restores ethical autonomy, pluralism, and gender justice inside Islamic thought.
dialecticalTension: Replaces authoritarian textual literalism with dialogical hermeneutic reason.
historicalContext: Rethinking the Qur’an: Towards a Humanistic Hermeneutics (2004).

citations.author: Nasr Hamid Abu Zayd
citations.work: Rethinking the Qur’an: Towards a Humanistic Hermeneutics

label: Reinforced historical-linguistic foundations for gender-egalitarian Qur’anic hermeneutics
description: Wadud’s tawhidic hermeneutics and Abu Zayd’s humanistic hermeneutics jointly established rigorous textual methodologies challenging patriarchal exegesis.
dialecticalTension: Converges Arabic semiotic critique with Islamic feminist theology.
